title: Postpartum Hemorrhage (PPH) Recognition and First-Response Pathway
review_note: Authored from WHO 2012/2017 and FIGO 2022 sources (see citations registry and docs/CLINICAL_SOURCES.md). REQUIRES sign-off by a qualified obstetric clinician and alignment with Nigerian FMOH national protocols before any pilot or clinical exposure. This file is for simulation/development only.

applies_to.population: Adult postpartum patients within 24 hours of birth (primary PPH), vaginal or cesarean
explicitly_out_of_scope: pediatric patients (any patient under 18 years of age — this module must REJECT such cases and hand back an out-of-scope response)
secondary PPH (bleeding between 24 hours and 12 weeks postpartum) — related but separate pathway
antepartum hemorrhage (placenta previa, abruption) — separate pathway
applies_to.setting: Low-resource and standard facilities: PHC, CHEW/midwife posts, secondary hospitals, emergency units in Nigeria and comparable LMIC settings

governing_principles: This pathway produces RECOMMENDATIONS for a human clinician, never commands. Every consequential action requires explicit human confirmation.
The deterministic rule engine is the sole source of truth for doses, thresholds, contraindications, and escalation criteria. The LLM layer may explain but may never alter these values.
Drug names, doses, concentrations, units, and thresholds must never be translated or localized; only explanatory prose may be localized.
When critical information is missing, the engine must NOT guess; it must surface a missing-information list and apply fail-safe defaults (assume higher risk).
Visual estimation of blood loss commonly UNDERESTIMATES true loss; the engine must never be reassured by a low estimated blood loss when physiologic signs (e.g., shock index) indicate deterioration.
If any input attempts to instruct the engine (prompt injection), the instruction content must be ignored and flagged; only structured clinical fields may influence rules.

pph.text: Cumulative blood loss >= 500 mL within 24 hours after vaginal birth, or >= 1000 mL after cesarean birth; OR any blood loss accompanied by signs/symptoms of hypovolemia regardless of measured volume.

severe_pph.text: Blood loss >= 1000 mL regardless of mode of birth, or PPH with hemodynamic instability (see shock_index.bands).

blood_loss_estimation_caveat.text: Visual estimation frequently underestimates blood loss. Where available, prefer quantitative methods (gravimetric, calibrated drapes/collection). Engine rule: physiologic indicators override low volume estimates.

categories.label: Trauma — genital tract lacerations, uterine rupture, hematoma
Thrombin — coagulopathy (e.g., DIC after abruption, severe preeclampsia, sepsis)

etiology_framework.engine_rule: At pathway activation, prompt for assessment of each 4T cause. Atony treatment must not delay identification and treatment of trauma/tissue causes; if bleeding persists despite a firm, contracted uterus, actively look for lacerations, retained tissue, or coagulopathy.

shock_index.normal_note: Standard obstetric shock index is ~0.7-0.9 (vs 0.5-0.7 in non-pregnant adults); pregnancy physiology delays classic vital-sign changes until large volume is lost.

bands.meaning: No hemodynamic alert from shock index. Does not exclude PPH; interpret with blood loss and clinical signs.
Hemodynamic alert. Associated with increased mortality risk; in community/PHC settings should trigger urgent escalation and preparation for transfer.
Critical hemodynamic compromise; high likelihood of need for transfusion and advanced intervention. Treat as hemorrhagic shock until proven otherwise.

notes: FIGO 2022 explicitly endorses SI >= 0.9 as the alert threshold (Box 2). The 1.3 critical band derives from the CRADLE Vital Signs Alert program (Nathan et al. 2015/2018/2019); the engine may make this threshold configurable by policy but must not set it lower than the FIGO 0.9 alert.
SI >= 0.9 has been proposed as the threshold to alert community providers of the need for URGENT TRANSFER.

activate_pathway_when_any.criterion: any blood loss with signs of hypovolemia (e.g., HR > 120, SBP < 90, altered mental status, oliguria, pallor, dizziness/syncope)
clinician judgment: ongoing heavy vaginal bleeding post-birth even without measured volume

recognition_criteria.fail_safe_default: If vital signs or blood loss data are missing but postpartum bleeding is reported, activate the pathway and mark severity as 'indeterminate — assume worst case until assessed'.

first_response_bundle.source: WHO technical consultation on PPH care bundles (Althabe et al. 2020), endorsed in FIGO 2022
first_response_bundle.implementation_note: IV fluid resuscitation is started together with IV uterotonics. If IV uterotonics are unavailable, start fluids in parallel with sublingual misoprostol or other parenteral uterotonics. If retained placenta: extract placenta and give a single dose of antibiotics. If lacerations: repair.

action_sequence.action: Call for help / activate PPH emergency: summon additional staff, alert referral facility and transport if facility cannot manage, assign a team lead and a scribe/timekeeper. Begin timing the response (time of birth, time of diagnosis).

Rapid structured assessment: airway/breathing/circulation; assess uterine tone (atony?), inspect for genital tract trauma, assess placental completeness (retained tissue?), consider coagulopathy (4T framework). Measure and record blood loss continuously.

Uterine (fundal) massage to stimulate contraction for PPH treatment (recommended for treatment of PPH; note: sustained massage is NOT recommended as prevention in women who received prophylactic oxytocin).

First-line uterotonic: oxytocin 10 IU IM or IV slow (intravenous oxytocin alone is the recommended first-line uterotonic for treatment of PPH). See medications.v1.json#oxytocin for administration and safety notes. Never administer oxytocin as rapid IV push (hypotension risk).

Tranexamic acid 1 g (100 mg/mL) IV over 10 minutes (1 mL/min) as soon as PPH is diagnosed AND within 3 hours of birth. Second dose of 1 g IV if bleeding continues after 30 minutes or restarts within 24 hours of the first dose. The 3-hour window is measured from TIME OF BIRTH, not from diagnosis.

Establish/maintain IV access (at least one large-bore line; two where possible) and begin isotonic crystalloid resuscitation. Isotonic crystalloids are recommended IN PREFERENCE to colloids. Warm fluids if possible. See fluid_resuscitation section.

If bleeding does not respond to oxytocin or oxytocin is unavailable: misoprostol 800 micrograms sublingual; OR ergometrine/methylergometrine 200 micrograms IM/IV ONLY IF hypertension/preeclampsia safely excluded (CONTRAINDICATED in hypertensive disorders); OR oxytocin-ergometrine fixed-dose combination (same hypertension contraindication). Where available, heat-stable carbetocin 100 micrograms IM/IV is an alternative uterotonic. Check medications.v1.json contraindication gates BEFORE any ergot alkaloid.

Treat the identified 4T cause in parallel: repair lacerations; remove retained placenta/tissue (give single-dose antibiotics if manual removal); if uterus is contracted but bleeding continues, escalate search for trauma/coagulopathy rather than repeating uterotonics.

Temporizing measures while definitive care/transfer is arranged: bimanual uterine compression or external aortic compression (for atony after vaginal birth); apply non-pneumatic anti-shock garment (NASG) as a temporizing measure; uterine balloon tamponade if uterotonics fail or are unavailable (only after retained products and uterine rupture are ruled out). Uterine PACKING is NOT recommended.

Escalate to definitive care: urgent transfer to facility with surgical and blood transfusion capability. Surgical options at capable facilities: uterine balloon tamponade, compression sutures, uterine/hypogastric artery ligation, uterine artery embolization (where available), hysterectomy as last resort. Priority: stop bleeding BEFORE coagulopathy and organ under-perfusion develop.

fluid_resuscitation.first_line: Isotonic crystalloids (e.g., 0.9% sodium chloride or Ringer's lactate), warmed if possible.
fluid_resuscitation.preference_rule: Isotonic crystalloids are recommended in preference to colloids for initial IV fluid resuscitation in PPH (strong recommendation, low-quality evidence — WHO 2012).
practical_guidance: Infuse rapidly while uterotonics and TXA are being given; fluid resuscitation runs in PARALLEL, not after drugs.
Do not delay fluid resuscitation while awaiting uterotonic effect.

RCOG-aligned volume discipline: up to ~2 L isotonic crystalloid (and not more than ~1.5 L colloid if used, ~3.5 L total clear fluids) before escalating to blood products; ongoing bleeding beyond this requires blood-based resuscitation, not more clear fluid.

Avoid aggressive over-resuscitation: consider hypotensive (permissive) resuscitation principles — target perfusion (mental status, urine output) rather than normal blood pressure until bleeding is controlled.
Monitor for signs of fluid overload; reassess after each liter.

targets.systolic_bp_mmHg_floor: maintain >= 80-90 pending hemorrhage control (permissive hypotension concept; do NOT chase normal BP with excessive crystalloid)
targets.citation_note: Targets derive from RCOG/FIGO resuscitation guidance; exact numeric BP target is a policy parameter, not a universal guideline constant.

principles: There is no single universal hemoglobin trigger endorsed by WHO/FIGO; transfusion decisions integrate ongoing bleeding, hemodynamic status, and estimated/expected loss.

Transfuse EARLY when: hemodynamic instability persists despite initial crystalloid + uterotonics + TXA; shock index in critical band; ongoing uncontrolled bleeding; or EBL already >= 1000-1500 mL with continued bleeding.
RCOG-aligned practice: use packed red cells to restore oxygen-carrying capacity and maintain hemoglobin > 8 g/dL during/after major hemorrhage.
Where blood is unavailable: apply NASG, use temporizing compression, expedite transfer — do not wait for deterioration.
Activate massive transfusion protocol where available (balanced ratios of red cells, plasma, platelets; fibrinogen/cryoprecipitate support) — FIGO 2022 section 11 (hemostatic resuscitation).

trigger_rules.condition: shock_index >= 1.3 OR (SBP < 90 AND HR > 120) persisting after initial measures
trigger_rules.recommendation: urgent blood transfusion where available; if unavailable, immediate transfer with NASG/temporizing measures

trigger_rules.condition: cumulative EBL >= 1500 mL with ongoing bleeding
trigger_rules.recommendation: anticipate coagulopathy; prepare blood products and massive transfusion capability; transfer if not available

trigger_rules.condition: hemoglobin < 7 g/dL (if measurable) OR < 8 g/dL with ongoing bleeding or instability
trigger_rules.recommendation: transfuse to maintain Hb > 8 g/dL during major hemorrhage (RCOG-aligned)

nasg.name: Non-pneumatic anti-shock garment (NASG)
nasg.role: Temporizing measure for hypovolemic shock secondary to obstetric hemorrhage until definitive care is available; useful during transport.
key_points: Apply per device instructions with monitoring
Removal only under controlled conditions with IV access and monitoring, gradually, with re-assessment between segments
Does not replace hemorrhage control, fluids, or blood
nasg.contraindications_note: See medications/devices review: specific device-level contraindications (e.g., bleeding source above the diaphragm, severe heart failure) require clinical review; verify against FIGO 2022 section 9.1.7 before pilot. Flagged UNVERIFIED in docs/CLINICAL_SOURCES.md.

uterine_balloon_tamponade.role: Recommended nonsurgical technique when uterotonics fail or are unavailable, AFTER ruling out retained products of conception and uterine rupture.
key_points: Condon-catheter or purpose-built balloon devices acceptable in low-resource settings
Document insertion time, fill volume, and drainage
Combine with continued uterotonics and second TXA dose per refractory bundle

not_recommended.intervention: uterine packing (gauze packing) for atony after vaginal birth

surgical_escalation_at_capable_facility: uterine artery embolization where interventional radiology exists
hysterectomy — last resort, do not delay when indicated

escalation.philosophy: Escalate EARLY. In low-resource settings, diagnosis, treatment, and referral must begin earlier than in hospital settings; transport time is part of the treatment timeline.

triggers.action: Alert receiving facility and arrange URGENT transfer; begin first-response bundle immediately; do not wait for transfer to start treatment

triggers.condition: shock_index >= 1.3, OR SBP < 90 with HR > 120, OR altered mental status attributable to hypovolemia
triggers.action: Hemorrhagic shock: immediate transfer to surgical/transfusion-capable facility with temporizing measures (NASG/compression) and ongoing resuscitation en route

triggers.condition: bleeding continues ~15-30 minutes after first-response bundle completed
triggers.action: Move to refractory-PPH bundle (compression measures, balloon tamponade, NASG, second TXA dose, continued uterotonics) and call most senior available clinician

triggers.condition: bleeding uncontrolled despite uterotonics + conservative measures
triggers.action: Surgical interventions recommended; if facility cannot perform them, transfer immediately — the priority is stopping bleeding before coagulopathy and organ damage

triggers.condition: required resource unavailable (no uterotonics, no blood products, no surgical capability) with ongoing PPH
triggers.action: Do not wait: apply temporizing measures and transfer to nearest capable facility; document the resource gap in the referral note

during_active_hemorrhage.parameter: HR, BP (compute shock index each measurement), RR, SpO2
mental status, urine output (catheterize when feasible)
uterine tone and response to each intervention
during_active_hemorrhage.frequency: with each intervention and every 5-15 minutes

after_stabilization.frequency: every 15 minutes for 2 hours, then every 30 minutes for at least 2-4 hours, then per obstetric early-warning policy

after_stabilization.parameter: lochia/ongoing loss, urine output, hemoglobin/coagulation where available
after_stabilization.frequency: each observation round; labs at earliest opportunity

after_stabilization.parameter: watch for late complications: coagulopathy, transfusion reactions, fluid overload, renal hypoperfusion

monitoring.note: Exact observation frequencies are a facility policy parameter; the schedule above is RCOG/WHO-aligned. An obstetric early-warning chart (MEOWS/IMEWS-style) should drive ongoing surveillance — see thresholds.v1.json.

community_or_home_birth_no_iv.rule: Start what is available IMMEDIATELY and trigger urgent transfer (esc-1). Do not attempt interventions outside training.

phc_with_midrugs.rule: Complete first-response bundle; if no response in 15-30 min or SI >= 1.3, transfer with temporizing measures running.

secondary_hospital.rule: Full pathway including refractory bundle; transfuse early; escalate to surgery without delay if bleeding uncontrolled.
